answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly audited task is proven fraudulent. The audit samples claims against independent evidence, so creating many aliases does not multiply the attacker’s chance of passing: every identity must fund its own bond and risk losing it. An oasis of cheap accounts therefore becomes costly; an opal-like stake and mirror checks make Sybil volume expensive rather than free.
